name: 1815 Prairie Avenue — Joseph Sears house (Arthur Meeker's from 1893)

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B stone dwelling (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1841 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: Refined from the district draft (T-2330) in place by T-3155 (piece 1 of T-1893), under the draft's own id, as a K01 stone-fronted house read off the two photographs Chicagology reproduces (chicagology_1815_sears_two_views: a square-on view and an oblique from the south-west, undated) against the 1911 sheet's plan: the front with its north pavilion under a steep hipped roof, the door under a bracketed hood up its stoop, the corner bay with its pierced stone balcony, the mansard with its gabled dormer, the stair projection and the canted bay on the flanks, and the rear range. The square-on view's camera and match record are in data/reference_views/sears_meeker_house_1815_prairie/; what it shows that is not built yet is open there.

documented_range.note: The 1904 target to the 1911 sheet that draws the house: the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). The photographs are undated; their dating is in the match record.

position.symbolic_location: 1815 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1815 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).
position.note: The front block's rear north corner: lot frame u 17.5, v -7.12 (the draft's frame point u 7.25, v -1.12 through its own rotation), where the 1911 sheet's trace (s28fp-1815-b1) runs the north wall behind the stair projection (v -7.07 to -7.17) and the front's main plane at u 34.96. The draft's fit of the sheet stands behind it (its georeference's independent check 1.47 m RMS). Rotation 179.45 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The front block read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s28fp-1815-b1 p1) in the lot frame: the front's main plane at u 34.96, the north wall at v -7.12 and the south wall at v 3.35, 10.47 m along the front; 17.46 m deep to lot u 17.5, so the sheet's canted south-flank bay (u 18.1-25.6) stands on it. The stair projection on the north flank, the corner bay, the canted flank bay and the rear range (to u 9.6) stand on it as K08 bays and a K01 rear wing.

stories.note: Two wall storeys over a raised basement under a mansard, read off the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px): the 1911 sheet's '3B' counts the mansard storey.

construction.note: The 1911 sheet colours the whole house blue, 'stone'; the photograph shows a smooth light ashlar street front (the 1973 landmarks report: 'yellow limestone'). K01 lays stone on the street front only, so the flanks and rear stand in brick: the photograph's rock-faced south flank is open in the match record.

principal_floor_m.note: The door's threshold at y 915 px on the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px).

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A stone front's thickness inside the K01 contract's range; no picture shows a reveal deep enough to read it.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: The K01 brick flank's thickness; the flanks are not read (their stone is open in the match record).

service_wall_brick.note: K01 lays the flanks and the rear in brick; the 1911 sheet colours the house stone and the oblique shows a rock-faced south flank, so the brick is a stand-in, buff for the light stone it stands in for.

stair_tread_m.note: The stoop's treads; the photograph shows the flight end-on.

roof_pitch_deg.note: The mansard's upper deck, above every view's sight line.

roof_covering.note: Slate on the mansard's faces and the pavilion's roof, laid in plain courses, on the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px) and the oblique; the deck above the sight line in painted standing-seam tin, and the flashing, are reconstructed.

window_kit.note: K06's two-over-two sash for the flat-headed lights; the photograph's principal-storey windows have leaded upper lights the kit does not carry, open in the match record.

stone_front.note: Smooth coursed ashlar in light stone across the whole street front on the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px), its basement storey laid in two broad courses under a plinth course at the principal floor (K02's channelled base, its channels 18 mm: a finer joint than the print can show, within tolerance). The fabric is K02's Lemont limestone for the 1973 landmarks report's 'yellow limestone' (a secondary reading); its exact quarry is reconstructed. T-3562: the south flank (K01's north wall) is the same stone, rock-faced: on the oblique photograph (the right of the two views, x 1605-1790 px) it reads dark and broken against the smooth front, its faces catching the light stone by stone, where the build laid it in buff common brick. It is laid on the front's beds in the profile's rock face (stone_front.flanks); the print lays it as broken-coursed random ashlar, the build as even courses on the front's lines, a joint pattern under a visitor's notice. That the flank is the front's Lemont stone and not another is inferred from the one reading of the fabric.

street_front_trim.note: Flat-headed openings in both storeys on the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px).

wall_head.note: A deep stone cornice on blocks over a dentil course at the second storey's head, y 357-430 px on the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px). T-3561: enlarged, the square-on print draws under the corona a close row of carved stone consoles, scrolled, with dark sunk panels between them and a rosette over each, standing on a plain frieze: twelve across the main front south of the pavilion (x 447-852 px, about 35 px or 0.49 m apart), each about 32 px (0.45 m) high and 12 px (0.17 m) wide, their feet at y 432 px (8.5 m) and the corona's soffit at about y 400 px (9.0 m); the oblique (the right print) carries the same row round the south-west corner and along the south flank. Built as K10's scrolled console in the walls' stone (wall_head.blocks, T-3186, as 1901's), 0.45 m high and 0.17 m wide at no more than 0.5 m apart, their tops under the corona's soffit, standing on a frieze 0.32 m under the cornice's foot, the most the upper storey's lintels leave under it, so the consoles' feet stand at 8.39 m against the print's 8.5 m (the build's corona stands about 0.15 m under the print's, within tolerance); the projection (0.19 m) is the most the corona's soffit covers, and the carving is the kit's generic scroll. The rosettes over the consoles are not built.

roof_form.note: A slated mansard over the front with a gabled dormer, and the north pavilion's own steep hipped roof, on the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px).

stoop_width_m.note: The stoop between its newels, x 165-420 px less the posts on the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px).

entrance_bay.note: The door at the north end of the front, in the pavilion's south half (x 288-393 px on the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px)); K01 names the footprint's v = 0 wall 'south', and on this east-side house that is the real north.

north_bays.note: The south flank as the oblique (the right of the two views) shows its front half: two window columns behind the corner bay; the rest of it is not seen.

rear_bays.note: The rear wall is hidden by the rear range.

basement_lights.note: The barred basement lights under the street window, x 490-575 px, y 1030-950 px on the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px).

chimneys.note: Two tall stacks on the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px): the north one over the stair projection behind the pavilion (x 85-130 px) (T-3562: read through the solved square-on camera its shaft, x 145-192 px at 29.8 m from the eye, centres about 0.33 m north of the north wall's line, over the stair projection, and its head is bare, a stone cap with no pot on it; it is built on the north wall's cornice, astride the wall line with its outer face at the cornice's 0.45 m edge (v -0.075), the furthest out K01 carries a stack on a house with no side parapet, about 0.25 m short of the print's, and it names its own pots as none) and the south one over the south flank near the front (x 785-820 px, also the oblique's broad stack). Their exact plans are reconstructed. T-3561: the south stack read off both prints and rebuilt. Triangulated through the two solved cameras (its south-west arris at x 830 px on the square-on and x 1765 px on the oblique), its west face stands about 1.6 m back from the front and its south face in line with the print's main south wall, which the oblique shows standing about 0.75 m inside the corner bay's south face (the open set-out in the match records): so it is the stack 'carried up from the flank wall past the mansard' of the oblique, standing on the south cornice. The build's south wall is still flush with the bay, so the stack stands on that wall's cornice (on_cornice, v 10.4), its west face at u 15.86, and moves with the wall when the set-out is built. Its plan, 1.1 m along the flank by 0.75 m, is the oblique's 60 px south face and the square-on's 50 px west face at their depths. Its head is read off both prints: the corbelled head's foot at about 13.6-13.8 m, the cap's top at about 14.3-14.5 m (top_m 14.45), the kit's tall clay pot on each of three flues to about 15.2 m (the oblique's pots reach 15.16 m). The pots stand in a row back from the street, so the stack is turned (across 'x'), and it names its own three flues where the north stack keeps two. Both stacks are K15's stone stack, its courses overridden by the head the print draws (three corbel courses, a 0.15 m cap): the oblique's lit west face is as pale as the stone front and the square-on shows it coursed. The sunk panels the oblique draws on its south face are not built: K15 lays a panel's recess in brick, so on a stone stack they would read as brick strips (open in the match record).

rainwater.note: No downpipe is visible on the front; one on the north flank and one at the rear.

entrance_kit.note: A panelled door under a transom (the house number '1815' on it) up a stoop between stone newels, on the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px). T-3562: over the door the photograph draws a stone pediment on two small carved brackets: its raking cornice's apex at y 621 px (5.86 m over grade) under a carved finial to y 592 px (6.27 m), its foot at y 690 px (4.9 m), its ends at x 305 and 487 px (2.55 m apart), the brackets at y 720-745 px (4.1-4.5 m) beside the transom. Built as K01's bracketed door hood with a pediment in place of the railing, in the front's stone: soffit 4.85 m (K01's 0.35 m over the 2.70 m door's head), apex 5.77 m, finial to 6.07 m, the brackets 0.4 m deep. It is built 1.72 m wide, not 2.55 m, because the build's pavilion stands 2.2 m wide north of the door where the photograph's 4 m pavilion carries the door in its south half (open in the match record): a wider hood would run into the pavilion's south cheek. The stoop's cheeks sweep down to a square stone newel at each foot under a cap and a ball knob (x 230-265 and 445-480 px, about 0.5 m square), read off the same print; their heights reconstructed within K07's swept-cheek ranges. The front yard is the lot's: the street line at lot u 44.29 m, the front at 34.96 m.

bays.note: Read off the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px) against the 1911 sheet (s28fp-1815-b1): the pavilion across the front's north end, carried up an attic storey past the main cornice under its own steep hipped roof (T-3156: its paired lights x 200-325 px and y 390-250 px, its eave at y 210 px, 11.6 m; the main eave stopping square at its cheeks, 0.3 m in from the north corner, K08's least pier to a corner, 2.2 m wide to stand clear of the entrance, which puts the attic over the print's within about 0.5 m): the photograph's quoined pavilion runs x 100-390 px (4.0 m) with the door in its south half, and K01 cannot cut a door through a projection, so it is built 2.45 m wide north of the door, its steep roof centred 0.75 m north of the photograph's (x 148-340 px), open in the match record; the one-storey corner bay at the south-west corner (x 600-845 px), its north cheek canted, a stone balcony with pierced panels on it; on the north flank the sheet's stair projection 0.86 m behind the front, 1.55 m out on the sheet and built 1.2 m out, K08's deepest pavilion (its face in shadow at x 45-100 px), and on the south flank the sheet's canted bay 9-13 m behind the front (lot u 18.1-25.6), its storeys reconstructed. The sheet draws no corner bay and a one-storey projection north of centre on the front instead; which is 1904's is open in the match record (the Heun remodel of 1902).

mansard.note: The slated mansard's curb under its cresting at y 150 px (12.4 m) on the square-on photograph (the left of the two views, Chicagology; 71.5 px/m on the front's plane, grade at y 1040 px), 2.9 m over the wall head; the gabled dormer centred at x 535 px, its sash x 498-580 px and y 345-230 px; a gabled dormer on the south flank in the oblique. The pavilion's steep roof (apex y 75 px, 13.5 m) is K01's hipped crown over it, raised by T-3156 onto the attic storey's wall head: its eave at y 210 px (11.6 m, 2.35 m over the main eave), the crown's eave 0.5 m past the attic's face (the print's x 165-360 px), its faces at 52 degrees so the apex stands about 13.8 m (the print's apex 13.5 m, read in front of the ridge's set-back). T-3562: the south flank's dormer read off the oblique, where it stands just east of the tall south stack (the stack's shaft x 1740-1820 px, the dormer's gable x 1820-1880 px): its centre about 1.4 m behind the stack's (the stack's 1.1 m shaft spans 80 px there), at 13.9 m from the rear, its body clear of the stack (it stood at 9.0 m, read off no picture, and so out of the oblique's frame). T-3562: the curb's iron cresting, the pavilion's cross and the street dormer re-read off the square-on print (66.7 px/m on the mansard's face): along the curb a pierced iron band, its top rail a dark line at y 146-150 px with hung ornaments under it and its foot on a dark line at y 178 over the slates, about 0.45 m, the sky showing over its rail and no deck behind it; built as the K10 kit's iron cresting 0.45 m high on the street curb and the south flank's (K01's north side; the oblique shows the curb under its cresting there), stopped short either side of the pavilion's crown where the crown stands through the curb (k01_mansard_deck.crown_gap); its pattern, hung trefoils in the print, is the kit's. On the crown's apex a cross over a square block and a flared cap, y 30-93 px, about 0.9 m: the block about 0.14 m across, the cap about 0.4 m, the cross's head from 0.6 of its height, its arms near the top (k01_mansard_deck.cross). The street dormer: its light y 230-347 px, about 1.7 m (it was built 1.35, its head 27 px low), built 1.65 m with a 0.05 m frieze between the surround's head and the gable's foot, the gable pitched 42 degrees (the print's foot at y 187 px and apex at y 135, a 52 px rise; the build's 50 degrees rose 68). The print's gable rises through the curb's cresting, about 0.15 m more light and frieze than the kit allows: it holds a lower-face dormer's head 0.1 m under the curb, and this one stands at 3.09 m against the curb's 3.2, and on the apex a finial y 93-130 px, about 0.45 m (a three-lobed iron fleur-de-lis in the print, built as the dormer ornament's turned finial).

rear_wings.note: The 1911 sheet draws the house three storeys deep to lot u 9.6, against the coach house: the range behind the front block (lot u 9.6-17.5) stands three storeys under a tin deck. The sheet colours it stone; K01 lays a wing in brick.

boundary.note: T-3206 (the owner, 2026-10-27: walks, gates and boundaries to the pictures). The square-on photograph (chicagology_square_on.json) shows no fence: a low stone coping along the inner edge of the public walk, and a square stone post about 0.9 m high either side of the walk where it leaves the stair, the walk running straight out between them. K11's stone coping wall, 0.25 m, on the parcel's street line (9.33 m from the front; data/street_grid/1904.json prairie_1815), the posts as 0.3 m runs 0.9 m high. Through the solved camera the posts stand at s 1.96-2.22 and 3.83-4.10 (x 186-214 and 386-414 px on the 2000 px print); they are laid at s 2.16-2.46 and 4.26-4.56, square to the stair's axis (s 3.36), 0.2-0.45 m from that reading (recorded in the match record). The parkway's stone posts at the curb are not this boundary.

yard.note: T-3206 (the owner, 2026-10-27: walks, gates and boundaries to the pictures).
